thesis_statement: Cheniere is the scaled U.S. LNG exporter converting long-term contracted volumes into cash: raised 2026 guidance on strong margins (Adjusted EBITDA to $7.9-8.4B), CCL Stage 3 trains substantially complete, and 5 mtpa of FERC-authorized capacity expansion plus the SPL expansion EPC contract with Bechtel - a contracted-growth compounder whose earnings still swing on global gas spreads.

base.summary: Full-year 2026 lands within the raised guidance as Stage 3 trains ramp to the tightened 53-54 mtpa production forecast, and buybacks plus the growing dividend compound per-share value.
drivers: CCL Stage 3 Midscale Trains 1-6 substantially complete; Train 7 first LNG imminent
raised FY26 guidance: Adjusted EBITDA $7.9-8.4B, DCF $5.3-5.8B
capital returns ($550M buybacks in Q2; $0.555/quarter dividend)

bull.summary: Global LNG demand (AI data-center power, Asian restocking) keeps TTF/Henry spreads wide, the FERC-authorized +5 mtpa expansion and SPL Stage V are sanctioned, and per-share value compounds through the cycle.
drivers: FERC authorization to increase CCL Stage 3 + Trains 8&9 capacity by ~5 mtpa
SPL Expansion Phase 1 EPC contract with Bechtel (May 2026)

bear.summary: Global gas spreads normalize (Henry up, TTF/JKM down) compressing margin per cargo, new capacity from U.S. peers floods the late-decade market, and the ~35-confidence band offers little timing protection.

key_risks: Margin structure is spread-dependent despite long-term contracts: a wide variance in net income (Q2 +$3.07B against a six-month loss of $434M) shows derivative-mark volatility that headline earnings do not describe.
Late-decade LNG supply wave (including Cheniere's own 8&9 and SPL expansions) is the structural risk to the post-2028 margin environment.
The band is narrow (~3% wide) with reference confidence 35 - it offers little statistical timing information.
Growth capital ($1.1B in Q2 alone) means distributable cash lags EBITDA; per-share compounding depends on execution discipline.

A major expansion sanction (SPL Stage V or Trains 8&9) is cancelled or materially delayed.

catalysts.event: Midscale Train 7 first LNG production (company: imminent as of the Q2 release)

evidence.claim: Q2 2026: revenues $5.73B; net income $3.07B (six-month net loss $434M - derivative-mark variance); Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA $1.80B; DCF $1.17B; raised FY26 guidance to Adjusted EBITDA $7.9-8.4B (from $7.25-7.75B) and DCF $5.3-5.8B; 184 cargoes exported; FY26 production forecast tightened upward to 53-54 mtpa; Midscale Train 6 substantial completion (June 2026), Train 7 first LNG imminent; FERC authorization for +~5 mtpa (CCL Stage 3 + Trains 8&9); SPL Expansion Phase 1 Bechtel EPC signed with limited notice to proceed; $550M buybacks and $0.555/share quarterly dividend in Q2; ~$1.1B growth capital deployed
Aggregator row current at Q2 2026 (period_end 2026-06-30, data_quality clean); trailing P/E 20.33, forward P/E 12.75, P/B 9.02, net debt $25.46B
